natural_language: A regional distribution-style transmission grid is modeled using the MATPOWER case74ds system. During a period of deferred maintenance, rotor winding insulation aging on the generator connected at bus 13 reduces its ability to operate at deep leading power factor, so the generator’s reactive lower limit is shifted upward, increasing its QMIN to a less-negative (or more-positive) bound consistent with degraded leading VAR capability. At the same time, a sequence of light-load hours leads operators to disconnect selected capacitor banks to avoid excessive reactive injection, and the operating policy is updated to permit a higher acceptable voltage ceiling at the sensitive node around bus 44, so bus 44’s VMAX is increased accordingly. Given these conditions, formulate a multi-period security-unconstrained DC optimal power flow using MOST with the DC network model enabled, driven by time-varying profiles across multiple periods, and solve for the expected dispatch and resulting marginal prices over the horizon while enforcing the modified generator and bus limits. Set opf.violation to 1e-06, use MOST with the DC model option as the solver configuration, and generate the corresponding MATPOWER code. All scenario-driven parameters are assigned using placeholder values of the form object_parameter_id, which represent post-modification values consistent with the specified scenario directions.

A regional transmission grid is modeled using the IEEE 141-bus system (case141). During a sustained heavy-load operating state driven by extreme pressure on the system (e.g., concurrent industrial ramp-up and widespread electrified heating), the real-power demand at bus 44 rises above its normal level and the reactive-power demand at bus 137 also increases as distribution-side voltage support becomes strained and more inductive loads come online. At the same time, a critical transformer on the corridor between buses 63 and 42 is pushed toward an overload condition, and operators increase its tap position to improve the low-side voltage profile and maintain acceptable margins, effectively increasing the branch tap ratio on that element. Given these conditions, formulate a DC security-constrained optimal power flow (DC-SCOPF) with N-1 line-contingency thermal constraints for all in-service branches that have RATE_A limits, and add a quadratic penalty on phase-angle differences across all in-service transmission lines with penalty weight beta = 10 to discourage excessive angular separation under stress. Set opf.violation to 1e-8, use MIPS as the solver, and generate the corresponding MATPOWER code. All scenario-driven parameters are assigned using placeholder values of the form object_parameter_id, which represent post-modification values consistent with the specified scenario directions.

A regional grid is modeled using the IEEE-style 22-bus test system (case22). Ahead of a major series of citywide events and holiday travel peaks, commercial districts concentrated around bus 13 experience a pronounced surge in both real and reactive consumption, increasing the active power demand and reactive power demand at that bus relative to the base case. At the same time, operators run a feasibility-focused stress assessment in which the voltage lower bound is intentionally ignored at bus 3 to avoid infeasibility being driven purely by minimum-voltage enforcement, effectively disabling the bus-3 lower voltage magnitude limit. Given these conditions, formulate a DC security-constrained optimal power flow (DC-SCOPF) with an N-1 set of transmission line outage constraints on all in-service branches that have nonzero thermal limits, and augment the optimization objective by adding a quadratic reactive power generation support cost term of the form sum(c_Q .* Qg.^2) to discourage excessive reactive dispatch. Set opf.violation to 1e-8, use MIPS as the solver, and generate the corresponding MATPOWER code. All scenario-driven parameters are assigned using placeholder values of the form object_parameter_id, which represent post-modification values consistent with the specified scenario directions.

natural_language: A regional transmission grid is modeled using the 85-bus test system (case85). Under a grid reliability directive that prioritizes nuclear units for must-run connection and dispatch, market offers are effectively adjusted so that selected marginal energy cost terms are reduced, reflecting preferential scheduling and lower perceived incremental cost for the units connected at buses 10, 8, and 2. In parallel, a fast-moving emergency operating posture is adopted after control-room alarms indicate heightened model uncertainty and limited telemetry quality, so operators intentionally simplify the network representation by disabling line charging and other second-order shunt effects, which is represented by setting the branch charging susceptance on the stressed corridor from bus 31 to bus 73 to zero. Given these conditions, formulate a multi-period DC optimal power flow using MOST with time-varying profiles, and additionally enforce PTDF-based two-sided chance constraints on all in-service branch thermal limits for a single stochastic injection source so that the absolute mean flow plus a Gaussian uncertainty margin remains within each line rating. Set opf.violation to 1e-07, use MIPS as the solver, and generate the corresponding MATPOWER code. All scenario-driven parameters are assigned using placeholder values of the form object_parameter_id, which represent post-modification values consistent with the specified scenario directions.

A regional grid is modeled using the IEEE 118-bus system (case118). During a period of unusually low distribution-level voltages and heavy reactive support needs, operators perform a coordinated set of on-load tap-changer adjustments to boost receiving-end voltages, which is represented by increasing the off-nominal tap ratio on the stressed transformer corridor from bus 9 to bus 116. At the same time, increasing flexibility and regulation demand from fast-changing net load (driven by variable renewables and responsive demand) leads operators to permit deeper peak-shaving operation, modeled by decreasing the minimum active power limit of the generator connected at bus 2. Given these conditions, formulate a DC multi-period security-constrained unit commitment style optimization using MOST (DC network model) with renewable and load profiles, storage modeling with cyclic state-of-charge, and the commitment-related extended generator data structure, then solve it using MATPOWER’s MOST workflow while enforcing the scenario-driven parameter changes. Set opf.violation to 1e-06, use MIPS as the solver, and generate the corresponding MATPOWER code. All scenario-driven parameters are assigned using placeholder values of the form object_parameter_id, which represent post-modification values consistent with the specified scenario directions.
